chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

One of you should not think that when he causes gladness to enter upon a believer, he has done so for him alone. No, by Allah, it is for us as well. And by Allah, it is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) as well.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The Ahl al-Bayt (implied by context of 'us')

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of making a believer happy according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the act of bringing joy to a believer from a simple social courtesy to a spiritual investment with cosmic significance, asserting that the reward extends beyond the individual to the Imams and ultimately to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). This underscores the Shia concept of the spiritual interconnectedness of the Ummah, where kindness to one member benefits the entire chain of divine authority. It serves as a practical reminder that social bonds are sacred transactions in the sight of God.
